thought.text: This is a newer Keycloak (form id `kc-form-login`, uses `credentialId`). Let me extract the action and POST the correct fields.

reasoning_content: This Keycloak login form does not use a csrf field — it's the newer Keycloak (v25+) with `credentialId`, `username`, `password`, `login` fields. The form id is `kc-form-login` (not `kc-login`). Let me extract the action properly and POST the correct fields.

action.command:
cd /tmp
ACTION=$(sed -n '/<form/,/<\/form>/p' kc.html | grep -oE 'action="[^"]+"' | head -1 | sed 's/action="//;s/"//' | sed 's/&/\&/g')
echo "action: ${ACTION:0:100}..."
# POST login with correct fields
curl -s -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -o after.html -w 'login POST: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n' \
  --data-urlencode "credentialId=" \
  --data-urlencode "username=spark@example.com" \
  --data-urlencode "password=SparkLocalPassw0rd!" \
  --data-urlencode "login=Sign In" \
  "$ACTION"
echo "--- after.html title/redirect hint ---"; grep -oE '<title>[^<]*</title>' after.html | head -1
